# local 0003: Compound literals in function bodies are initialized at the start of their block and not where they are evaluated

- Category: [Fixes](../../fix.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17192
- Recommended action: Apply the patch. It does not change literals in the initializers of declarations, which Related describes.
- Patch: [local-0003.patch](../../patches/local-0003.patch), commit [`d6323cfb5`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/d6323cfb5d9299594b407e44969baebf9b144d19). Applies to r17192 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

In function bodies, the objects of compound literals are initialized when control enters the
innermost block around the literal. By C11 6.5.2.5 a literal has the value of an unnamed object
that its initializer list initializes, so the initialization belongs where the literal is
evaluated. Literals whose initializers name a variable get the value that the variable had at
the start of the block. Literals under a `case` label are not initialized, because control does
not pass through the start of the body of a `switch`. The file below was compiled with
`sdcc -mmcs51 cl.c` on r17176 and run in ucsim.

```c
__xdata __at (0x7000) unsigned char res[2];

int g (unsigned char op, int x)
{
  int y = 0;

  switch (op)
    {
    case 0:
      y = x ? 4 : (int){3};
      break;
    }
  return y;
}

int m (int x)
{
  x = x + 1;
  return (int){x};
}

void main (void)
{
  res[0] = g (0, 0);            /* 3 expected */
  res[1] = m (1);               /* 2 expected */
}
```

`res` is `00 01`, where `03 02` is expected. It is `00 01` with `--model-medium`, `--model-large`,
`--stack-auto`, and `--model-large --stack-auto` too. For `g` the compiler prints warning 126 for
unreachable code and warning 84 for a variable that may be used before its initialization. The
loop `for (i = 0; i < 3; i++) s += (int){i + 1};` gives 3 for `s`, where 6 is expected. For a
literal in one of the three expressions of a `for` statement, the assembler rejects the output,
because the object does not get storage.

## Cause

`gatherImplicitVariables` in `src/SDCCast.c` appends the object of each compound literal to the
declarations of the innermost block around the literal. `gatherAutoInit` puts its initialization
at the start of that block, together with the initializations of the block's variables. In the
body of a `switch`, the start is in front of the first `case` label. `gatherImplicitVariables`
does not visit the three expressions of a `for` statement, which are not operands of its node.
The ports share this code.

## Fix

`gatherImplicitVariables` sets the new symbol flag `complitobj` on these objects and visits the
expressions of `for` statements. For an object with the flag, `gatherAutoInit` calls the new
function `placeCompLitInit`. It searches the tree of the block for the literal and puts the
initialization in front of the statement that evaluates it. When the literal is in the right
operand of `&&`, `||`, or the comma operator, in the second or third operand of `?:`, or in an
expression of a `for` statement, the initialization becomes the left operand of a comma operator
in that operand. It is then evaluated only when the literal is. Literals in the operand of
`sizeof` are not initialized. The change is 87 lines in `src/SDCCast.c` and `src/SDCCsymt.h`.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/compound-literal-eval.c` has 19 assertions. Its literals are under a
`case` label, after a `goto`, in loop bodies, in operands that are not always evaluated, in the
controlling expressions of loops, and in an inline function. Some are used as lvalues. On r17192
with the earlier patches of the series, the test does not assemble for mcs51. A copy without the
literals in its `for` statement fails 8 assertions and then runs until the time limit of the
simulator, on mcs51-small and mcs51-large-stack-auto. With the patch the test passes on host,
stm8, ucz80, and mcs51 with the small, medium, large, and huge models and with `--stack-auto` for
the small and large models.

With the patch series of this report up to the patch for local 0001 applied to r17192, the
regression suite ran without a failure for these nine targets. The diagnostics suite ran without a
failure for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8. Among the other regression tests,
the code size differs with the patch only in five, which use compound literals: the GCC torture
test 20020206-2, bug-4151, bug-4157, bug-4228, and compound-literal. On each of the eight targets
other than host, they are together 1 to 64 bytes smaller. 20020206-2 evaluates a literal in a
loop of two iterations. Without the patch its function `foo` gets the argument 0x800 twice, which
the test accepts, and with the patch it gets 0x800 and 0x810.

## Related

- Literals in the initializer of a declaration are initialized in front of the initialization of
  that declaration, with and without the patch. The initializer is not in the tree of the block
  when `gatherAutoInit` runs. The initialization also happens when the literal is not evaluated.
  `int a = c ? (int){f ()} : 7;` calls `f` when `c` is 0.
- For `inline int f (int x) { return (int){x}; }` with a later `extern int f (int x);`, the code
  that the compiler inlines into a caller reads `_f_PARM_1`. The linker reports an undefined
  global, and with `--stack-auto` the assembler rejects the output. The patch does not change
  this. The `static inline` form is correct.
- Bug #4248 concerns the double initialization of a literal in the initializer of a declaration.
  Its patch and the patch for bug #4145, applied to r17176, do not change the results above.
